programs.name: Data Science, Minor

groups.title: Approved data-focused electives
notes: Select two or more courses overlapping with Computation, Application, Communication and Deliberation, focused on temporal, spatial or numerical data.
Other courses require approval from the Data Science Undergraduate Curriculum Committee. Special topics from other departments also require this approval.
BUAD 351 is listed without a title or live course link in the program requirements; its course details are unresolved.

rules: No restriction on the primary major paired with the minor.
Normally declare by the second semester of junior year.
Two courses may count toward both primary major and minor.
Published 18 hours is a nominal minimum; CSCI 141 is 4 credits and electives can vary in credit value. Prerequisites may require additional credits.

fit.summary: Add data analysis, visualization, ethics and AI skills to another major; apply evidence to questions in an existing field.

programs.name: Artificial Intelligence, Minor

groups.title: Restricted electives
notes: For DATA 440, the listed eligible topics are Graph Learning, Trustworthy AI and Natural Language Processing, each 3 credits.
CSCI 420 topics/prerequisites vary; ensure the selected section supplies the required credit total.

rules: Published requirement is 19 credits. Course prerequisites can add coursework beyond these 19 credits.
In particular DATA 301 requires DATA 201 plus an accepted linear algebra course plus DATA 210 or MATH 352; DATA 201 is not in the AI minor required-course table.

fit.summary: Add programming, logic, statistical research and machine learning foundations, then specialize through AI electives.

programs.name: Applied Artificial Intelligence (BA in Interdisciplinary Studies)

groups.title: Applied AI electives
notes: Six credits carrying the Applied AI attribute, or approved courses in other disciplines identified with the student advisor. The program page does not provide a closed list.

rules: The official award is a BA in Interdisciplinary Studies, managed by the Department of Data Science.
At least 120 credits are needed for the overall degree. The 30 hours covers the major, not all graduation requirements.

The PHIL 150 alternative is specifically identified by the program as Philosophy of Technology (4 credits). The generic PHIL 150 course record is First-Year Seminar with variable topics; arbitrary PHIL 150 sections are not verified equivalents.
Choosing the four-credit PHIL 150 topic produces 31 credits with the listed six elective credits.
AAI 101, AAI 301 and AAI 302 have their own catalog course records even though the undergraduate subject index omits an AAI listing; do not silently replace them with DATA 101, DATA 305 or DATA 415.

fit.summary: Use and evaluate AI tools in another field: agent design, coordinated AI workflows, research design, visualization, ethics and trustworthy AI.

programs.name: Data Science (BS in Data Science)

groups.title: Capstone
groups.subject: DATA
notes: One 400-level DATA course fulfills the capstone.
DATA 491 and DATA 495 cannot fulfill this requirement.
For students successfully completing honors, DATA 496 may fulfill it.
Courses used for the capstone cannot also supply track credits.

fit.summary: Design, build and implement AI algorithms and models that analyze complex data, recognize patterns and predict outcomes.
Develop software and algorithms for ingesting or analyzing large, frequently near-real-time data sources, with depth in computational efficiency.

groups.title: Data application methods
groups.subject: DATA
notes: Three DATA courses numbered 340 or higher with a significant component of analyzing datasets using Data Science techniques.
DATA 340 and DATA 440 may be repeated when topics differ.
DATA 491 cannot fulfill this track.
DATA 495 may count for students pursuing honors.
Eligibility is a content rule, not blanket approval of every DATA course numbered 340 or higher.

fit.summary: Build data pipelines, combine sensor and other data, make predictions and update models with real-time information.
Analyze large-scale geospatial data, including satellite and survey information.

rules: Select a track at major declaration; each track comprises three additional methods-oriented courses.
Track and capstone coursework must be distinct.
DATA 201 usually satisfies major computing proficiency; another course may be petitioned to the Data Science Undergraduate Committee.
DATA 202 usually satisfies major writing proficiency; another course may be petitioned to the same committee.
The published requirements table totals 36 hours. Alternatives with higher credits and prerequisite courses may increase the student total.

The DS minor overview still describes the BS as 40 credits with three tracks. The current BS requirements page explicitly publishes 36 hours and four track sections, including AI; the website should retain a visible catalog discrepancy note.

fit.summary: Build a broad foundation in AI, data modeling, databases, visualization, statistics and ethics, then deepen through a chosen methods track.

catalogIssues.text: DS minor overview says DS BS minimum 40 hours and three tracks. Current DS BS requirements say 36 hours and explicitly list four tracks, including Artificial Intelligence. Use the direct BS requirements while disclosing the discrepancy.

AAI major and DS AI track name AAI 101/301/302. DATA list separately names DATA 101/305/415. They are not interchangeable unless formally approved; AAI 301 and DATA 305 have different stated prerequisites.

AI minor nominal 19 credits omits DATA 201, which is required to enroll in DATA 301. A linear algebra course is also a DATA 301 prerequisite; DATA 209 is only an elective in the minor. Show prerequisite coursework separately.
AAI major specifies PHIL 150 Philosophy of Technology (4); generic catalog record is First-Year Seminar. Topic and approval need confirmation.
DS minor lists BUAD 351 without title/link, and no BUAD 351 record is in undergraduate BUAD catalog.
